project.summary: SSSF is a well-designed skeleton with an inverted verification story. The decision density is exceptional (rationale lives next to nearly every choice), the packaging is drift-free (templates byte-identical to the live tree), and the observability UI is the most complete part. But the factory's core is unproven: 1 of 12 workflows has ever run, none since the backend swap to claude_code/codex, there are zero tests anywhere, the in-repo quality blocks are echo-placeholders, and the engine has no timeout or stall detection — a hung CLI blocks an ADW forever while the documented escape hatch (just kill) does not exist. The doc layer still describes the pre-swap 'pi v1' architecture in at least four places.

contradictions: The factory's core loop is unproven in its current form: 1 of 12 workflows has ever run, none since the backend swap, zero tests exist, and the in-repo quality blocks are echo placeholders — a verification factory that is itself unverified.

Stall handling is split brain: the engine has no timeout at all (a hung CLI blocks forever at the blocking stdout loops), the documented escape hatch 'just kill' does not exist in any justfile, and the only real stall tooling is the visualizer's manual kill/nudge added 2026-08-13.

The doc layer describes the pre-swap architecture: 'pi v1 / agent_cc stubbed' persists in SKILL.md:9, update_modules.md:17, sssf_overview.md:26, and the backends plan doc, while claude_code is the shipping default.
'Read-only observability' is claimed in three places while the server now exposes three mutating endpoints (archive, kill, nudge).
Quality-failure philosophy contradicts itself: adw_quality.py:37-38 fails the phase on a failing block; adw_build_test.py:12-19 declares failing blocks must not fail the phase.
gates.py resolves artifact paths against the operator's cwd while agents write at run.repo_root — correctness depends on where the script was launched.
